architecture_decisions.recommendation: Created build-constrained files to separate syscall-dependent code from the main codebase using Go's build tag system
architecture_decisions.rationale: The syscall package is not available in WASM environments, causing compilation failures. By using build constraints (`//go:build`), we can conditionally compile different implementations for different target architectures while maintaining a clean API surface.
alternatives_considered: Using runtime checks with build tags in the same file
Creating a separate package for platform-specific code
Using interface-based abstraction with platform-specific implementations

architecture_decisions.recommendation: Extracted the syscall.Exec call into a wrapper function with consistent signature across platforms
architecture_decisions.rationale: This approach maintains a clean separation between the core application logic and platform-specific implementations. The wrapper function provides a uniform interface that can be called from BaseApp.Restart() without conditional logic, improving code readability and maintainability.
alternatives_considered: Using conditional compilation directives within the same function
Using function pointers initialized based on build tags

architecture_decisions.recommendation: Returned errors.ErrUnsupported for the WASM implementation to clearly indicate the operation is not available
architecture_decisions.rationale: In WASM environments, process execution is fundamentally impossible due to security constraints. Returning a clear, standard error (errors.ErrUnsupported) communicates this limitation explicitly rather than trying to fake functionality or return a generic error.
alternatives_considered: Returning nil and logging a warning
Creating a custom error type for WASM-specific limitations

architecture_decisions.recommendation: Removed the direct syscall import from base.go and made it conditional through build-constrained files
architecture_decisions.rationale: Direct imports of platform-specific packages in shared code prevent cross-compilation. By moving the import to build-constrained files, we eliminate the unconditional dependency while preserving functionality for supported platforms.
alternatives_considered: Using blank imports with build constraints
Creating a separate package with platform-specific implementations
Using reflection to dynamically load the syscall package

tickets.title: WASM Build Compatibility - Syscall Abstraction
tickets.description: Create platform-specific implementations for syscall.Exec to enable WASM compilation

implementation_summary:
The implementation addresses WASM compilation compatibility by abstracting the platform-specific syscall.Exec functionality behind build constraints. The key change was removing the direct syscall import from core/base.go and replacing the syscall.Exec call with a wrapper function 'exec'. This wrapper is then implemented in two separate files with Go build tags: syscall.go for standard builds (excluding WASM) and syscall_wasm.go for WASM builds.

This approach follows the Go idiom of using build constraints for platform-specific code while maintaining a clean API. The standard implementation delegates to the actual syscall.Exec, preserving the original restart functionality for native builds. The WASM implementation returns errors.ErrUnsupported, acknowledging the fundamental limitation of process execution in browser environments.

The pattern used here is minimal and idiomatic - it doesn't introduce unnecessary abstraction layers but provides just enough separation to enable cross-compilation. This change integrates seamlessly with the existing codebase because it only affects the single point where syscall was used, and the function signature remains identical across implementations, ensuring backward compatibility for all non-WASM builds.
